messages:
jamal: Just merged PR #4823 (reduce kvcache lock). Main pipeline turned red immediately — smoke-e2e-gpu failed on kernel allocate. Link: https://ci.internal/red/1968001234
ci-bot: [pipeline] pipeline/main @1968001234 FAILED — smoke-e2e-gpu (step: gpu-smoke, exit code 137)
jamal: logs show: 
```
ERROR: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory at alloc_kernel.c:123
Backtrace: ...
```
olivia: @jamal ping — who owns that area now? @alex_k added the change, right?
alex_k: I authored the PR, yep. I ran unit + gpu-smoke locally but didn't hit OOM. 
maria_g: Can someone kick a rerun so we see if it's flaky? /rerun smoke-e2e-gpu
ci-bot: rerun queued (job id 1968001240) — triggered by maria_g
jamal: rerun in progress. If it flakes again, we should bisect. This feels like an allocation regression from the recent kernel selector changes.
ci-bot: rerun finished (1968001248): FAILED — same OOM in alloc_kernel.c
alex_k: ugh. Reproduced by CI. I'm going to try reproducing with a bigger trace and reduced batch sizes locally.
maria_g: Can we run a quick bisect range: main~20..main? I can start the bisect job: `scripts/ci-bisect --target smoke-e2e-gpu --start main~20 --end main`
olivia: tagging infra and runtime: @sre-oncall @infra-team — kernel alloc OOM spike after few merges.
sre-oncall: I'll take lead. Starting automated bisect now and collecting the failing commit list. Will update in ~30m :hourglass_flowing_sand:
jamal: For short-term unblock, can we reduce the test batch to avoid OOM and unblock dependent PRs? I can open a tiny PR to lower batch from 8->4 in the smoke test.
alex_k: I prefer bisect first to avoid masking the real issue. If bisect takes too long, we can fall back to temp test tweak.
maria_g: Bisect job started: job 1968001260. Command: `./scripts/ci-bisect --jobs=10 --cmd='yarn test:smoke --gpu'`
sre-oncall: Bisect found a candidate commit: `commit 9f3c2a` that introduced a kernel selection change. I'm re-running the failing test on that exact commit now.
ci-bot: bisect result (1968001298): suspect commit 9f3c2a (author: taylor) — test fails consistently there.
olivia: Good detective work. @taylor or infra, can we revert or patch the commit?
jamal: I'll draft a revert PR for 9f3c2a to restore previous kernel fallback behavior.
alex_k: If revert is risky, another option is to add a defensive allocation cap in the runtime as a hotfix. Depends on how invasive revert is.
sre-oncall: For now, I'm marking main as a blocking incident and pushing a rollback candidate. Updating the incident board and notifying release leads. :rotating_light:
maria_g: Thanks all — keeping dependent merges on hold. Will update once revert PR lands or we have a clean main.
jamal: created PR #4830 to revert 9f3c2a — link: https://git.internal/PR/4830 — requesting urgent review from infra/runtime.
olivia: Reviewing now, will merge on green if CI passes after revert.
sre-oncall: Close loop: once revert merges, we should run a smoke run against the affected configs and run an extended soak overnight.
alex_k: I'll follow up with a postmortem and a test coverage addition to catch kernel-selection regressions.
maria_g: Thanks everyone. Leaving monitoring alerts set. If anyone sees more pipeline red, ping this thread. :thumbsup:
